title: VertiAdaptor: Online Kinodynamics Adaptation for Vertically Challenging Terrain
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Off-road dynamics shift with terrain, while gradient-based adaptation can be too slow for onboard planning.
mechanism: Embed elevation and appearance, learn neural-ODE basis functions offline, then fit their mixture coefficients by least squares using new trajectories.
evidence_scope: Prediction and adaptation comparisons on simulated terrain; MPPI trials, five per setting; a 70.3-second physical dataset split into 28.1-second adaptation and 42.2-second evaluation segments.
writing_move: Connect a deployment resource constraint to the mathematical design, then disclose the counterintuitive result that continual updates underperform one-time adaptation.
research_lesson: Evaluate model accuracy, update latency, and closed-loop success separately: improvement in one does not guarantee another.
reviewer_question: Does adaptation use only causally available experience, and how does performance change when recent terrain differs from upcoming terrain?

evidence_pages.observation: Online adaptation estimates coefficients in a frozen basis, not all network weights.
On high terrain, one-time VA succeeds 4/5, periodic VA 1/5; real-world evidence evaluates prediction rather than navigation.

limits_or_counterexample: Table II gives MAML lower high-terrain MSE; periodic adaptation suffers recent-history mismatch. One-time adaptation uses samples across the new environment.
citation: Tong Xu, Chenhui Pan, Aniket Datar, and Xuesu Xiao . VertiAdaptor: Online Kinodynamics Adaptation for Vertically Challenging Terrain . Accepted by 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).

title: Traverse the Non-Traversable: Estimating Traversability for Wheeled Mobility on Vertically Challenging Terrain
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: High-fidelity 6-DoF rollouts are expensive, and conventional traversability labels exclude terrain that capable wheeled robots can cross.
mechanism: Build terrain costs from roll/pitch, command-realization mismatch, and prediction residuals; distill patch-wise estimates into a map that guides MPPI or A*.
evidence_scope: 139 minutes of physical teleoperation supply learning data. Ten trials per method on a reconfigured indoor rock course compare TNT, TAL, and WMVCT; outdoor operation is a demonstration.
writing_move: Turn the surprising possibility of crossing supposedly non-traversable terrain into a precise computational bottleneck and an intermediate representation.
research_lesson: A simpler auxiliary representation can make a more accurate model useful within a real-time compute budget.
reviewer_question: Does orientation-averaged, state-independent terrain cost incorrectly reject patches traversable under particular approach speeds or headings?

evidence_pages.observation: Traversability is explicitly simplified to omit state and action dependence.
Patch costs are averaged over orientations before map reconstruction.
Successes are 9/10, 6/10, and 8/10; not every stability metric favors TNT.

limits_or_counterexample: Geometry alone omits deformability/semantics; the Table I absolute-pitch and delta-pitch values do not support a universal stability win.
citation: Chenhui Pan, Aniket Datar, Anuj Pokhrel, Matthew Choulas, Mohammad Nazeri, Tong Xu, and Xuesu Xiao . title: Robot Squid Game: Quadrupedal Locomotion for Traversing Narrow Tunnels
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Confined volumes require body adaptation beyond ground-only locomotion, but one policy can struggle across heterogeneous tunnel geometries.
mechanism: Procedurally generate four tunnel classes, train privileged specialists, then use tunnel-matched DAgger supervision and class-balanced replay to distill one depth-conditioned student.
evidence_scope: Simulation compares methods over 50 trials per tunnel/difficulty condition. Physical Go 2 testing uses ten trials per configuration, defining success as at least 80% traversal without external recovery.
writing_move: Enumerate three prior limitations, map architectural choices to them, and expose a privileged-training/deployable-sensing boundary.
research_lesson: Separate learning locomotion from learning noisy perception, while explicitly testing what changes at deployment.
reviewer_question: Are training exposure and compute matched when comparing multi-expert distillation against a single generalist and a circular-only teacher?

evidence_pages.observation: Class-conditioned distillation and balanced replay preserve specialized behavior.
Two-layer elevation ablation performs poorly; physical success differs from complete, collision-free traversal.

limits_or_counterexample: Structured primitives do not cover debris or junction networks. The reported energy quantity integrates absolute torque, not mechanical work or electrical energy.
citation: Amir Hossain Raj, Dibyendu Das, and Xuesu Xiao . Robot Squid Game: Quadrupedal Locomotion for Traversing Narrow Tunnels . Accepted by 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).

title: Fire as a Service: Augmenting Robot Simulators with Thermally and Visually Accurate Fire Dynamics
reading_depth: Main text read in full, including conclusion after extraction-order reference heading; references not close-read
problem: Robot simulators often render fire visually without modeling thermal hazards, whereas engineering fire solvers can be too slow for interactive control.
mechanism: Asynchronously bridge Fire-X and robot simulators through ROS 2, compositing depth-aware fire visuals and publishing thermal sensing/costmaps.
evidence_scope: Integration across three simulators; deterministic thermal-dose path walks; twenty teleoperated imitation-learning paths; reactive-control latency perturbations.
writing_move: Position a modular bridge between two mature tool families and make its synchronization tradeoff explicit.
research_lesson: Validate infrastructure with interoperability, latency, and downstream-use tests, not visual appeal alone.
reviewer_question: Which thermal accuracy is inherited from Fire-X validation, which is newly validated, and how does stale sensor data affect the intended operating envelope?

evidence_pages.observation: Control remains unpaused while fire observations may be stale; dose integrates irradiance over time.
Longer paths reduce dose, but the largest detour adds substantial distance for a small further dose reduction.
Two-second artificial latency breaks avoidance in the tested setup; no bidirectional robot-fluid interaction or heat damage is modeled.

limits_or_counterexample: Simulated avoidance and plausible radiation do not establish hardware survivability. Behavioral-cloning illustration includes replayed sensor inputs rather than broad held-out deployment statistics.
citation: Anton R. Wagner, Madhan Balaji Rao, Helge Wrede, Sören Pirk, and Xuesu Xiao . Fire as a Service: Augmenting Robot Simulators with Thermally and Visually Accurate Fire Dynamics . Accepted by 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).

title: CORAL: COntextual Reasoning And Local Planning in A Hierarchical VLM Framework for Underwater Monitoring
reading_depth: Main text and prompt/pseudocode appendix read in full; references not close-read
problem: Per-step VLM control is slow, dynamics-unaware, and susceptible to accumulating navigation errors during reef monitoring.
mechanism: A VLM selects tracked cluster centroids or discrete waypoints; geometric verifiers reject bad choices, event triggers limit queries, and DDP-MPPI executes continuously.
evidence_scope: Ten synthetic reef environments with ground-truth perception, component removals, topology breakdown, and a representative controlled-pool deployment.
writing_move: Three specific failure modes become three architectural responsibilities; failures receive their own analysis rather than being hidden in average coverage.
research_lesson: Constrain a general model to decisions it can express reliably and delegate geometry/dynamics to explicit machinery.
reviewer_question: How much improvement survives realistic segmentation, depth, localization error, and VLM latency under matched wall-clock budgets?

evidence_pages.observation: Simulation uses noise-free perception; categorical centroid selection constrains VLM output.
Coverage rises from 80% to 94.28%; mission-time definitions account for different execution models.
Local verifiers cannot prevent globally looping branches; pool evidence is a representative trial.

limits_or_counterexample: Zero simulated collisions is not a safety guarantee. Pool coverage is approximate; open-water localization and changing environmental conditions remain future work.
citation: Zhenqi Wu, Yuanjie Lu, Xuesu Xiao , and Xiaomin Lin. CORAL: COntextual Reasoning And Local Planning in A Hierarchical VLM Framework for Underwater Monitoring . Accepted by 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).

title: Understanding Fire Through Thermal Radiation Fields for Mobile Robots
reading_depth: Main text and parameter appendix read in full; references not close-read
problem: Thermal images describe visible surfaces, not free-space radiative exposure along a robot path.
mechanism: Fuse thermal and depth data, localize a hot cluster, approximate a hemispherical source, and project inverse-square radiation with occlusion into an A* costmap.
evidence_scope: Controlled Spot demonstrations vary fire presence, caution, and shielding. Calorimetry and fuel consumption provide independent magnitude checks for a single propane source.
writing_move: Explain the sensing blind spot before introducing the representation; validate a model quantity independently of navigation visuals.
research_lesson: A useful physics-informed approximation needs calibrated units, explicit assumptions, and an error consequence expressed in task terms.
reviewer_question: How are radiative versus total power, empirical corrections, sensor saturation, and omitted convection propagated into the claimed safe-distance estimate?

evidence_pages.observation: Assumes 1200°C source temperature, empirical correction 0.4, and radiative fraction 0.35.
Modeled 10.79 versus measured 6.4 kW/m² implies 0.22 m safe-distance discrepancy in this test.

limits_or_counterexample: A single controlled source, assumed strength, and radiation-only model do not validate safety around arbitrary structural fires; low-cost thermal sensing saturates at 192.5°C.
citation: Anton R. Wagner, Madhan Balaji Rao, Xuesu Xiao , and Sören Pirk. Understanding Fire Through Thermal Radiation Fields for Mobile Robots . Accepted by 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).
venue_full: Accepted by 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)

title: TransCurriculum: Multi-Dimensional Curriculum Learning for Fast & Stable Locomotion
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Single-axis or history-blind curricula can learn speed without robustness to interacting terrain and dynamics factors.
mechanism: A transformer predicts outcomes from locally retrieved task histories and expands sampled bins over commands, terrain, friction, and payload while PPO trains locomotion.
evidence_scope: IsaacGym study; scheduler and dimensionality ablations; short zero-shot Go 1 trials over several surfaces. Literature speed comparisons involve different robot embodiments.
writing_move: Separate two proposed causes with two ablations: history for fast learning and multidimensionality for transfer/stability.
research_lesson: Distinguish peak simulation capability from transferable operating performance and from cross-paper comparisons.
reviewer_question: Are history inputs, training exposure, statistics, and baseline robots matched, and is the claimed transfer loss relative to command or achieved simulated speed?

evidence_pages.observation: Reported prior maximum speeds come from cited papers on different robots.
6.3 m/s belongs to command-only training; full curriculum reaches 5.8 m/s in simulation and 4.1 m/s hardware at a 5 m/s command.

limits_or_counterexample: Rock trials succeed only 50%; greater curriculum dimensionality lowers maximum simulated speed while improving transfer. Cross-platform speed ranking is contextual, not a controlled head-to-head benchmark.
citation: Prakhar Mishra, Amir Hossain Raj, Xuesu Xiao , and Dinesh Manocha. TransCurriculum: Multi-Dimensional Curriculum Learning for Fast & Stable Locomotion . Accepted by 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).
venue_full: Accepted by 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)

title: HUMEMBR: Learning Human Routines for Predictive Embodied Navigation
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Static spatial maps and unstructured long contexts poorly support persistent person-centered routine queries.
mechanism: Continuously caption observations and associate identities, then expose structured temporal/person/spatial retrieval functions to a language-model navigation agent.
evidence_scope: Twenty days and 31 hours of office observations support a frozen 200-question benchmark; six representative physical tasks have ten runs each. Main benchmark remains same-site.
writing_move: Define a missing task class, provide a benchmark, then test memory design, reasoning backbone, function budget, and embodied execution separately.
research_lesson: More context and more retrieval calls are not automatically better; measure accuracy against cost by query type.
reviewer_question: Are identity errors, absent-person hallucinations, observation sparsity, and consent/retention policies separately evaluated?

evidence_pages.observation: Method averages three seeds; computationally expensive full-context baseline uses one.
Ten calls outperform fifteen overall; full-context baseline remains stronger on some exact temporal/person questions.
Partial-occlusion tasks succeed 50%; consent, pseudonymization, restricted logs, and withdrawal rights are stated.

limits_or_counterexample: Persistent tracking creates privacy risks; target absence can provoke invented observations, and favorable same-site results do not establish cross-site generalization.
citation: Samira Huber, Klaas Pelzer, Duc M. Nguyen, Xuesu Xiao , and Sören Pirk. HUMEMBR: Learning Human Routines for Predictive Embodied Navigation . Accepted by 2026 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).

title: Narrate2Nav: Real-Time Visual Navigation with Implicit Language Reasoning in Human-Centric Environments
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Large VLM reasoning is costly and difficult to translate into precise real-time motion.
mechanism: Use multimodal future trajectories and generated narrations to train a teacher, then align a smaller RGB-history student through Barlow Twins pretraining and supervised trajectory prediction.
evidence_scope: Held-out offline trajectories, text-removal ablation, and four physical scenarios with ten trials each; the crowds scenario is omitted because all methods degrade.
writing_move: Convert a broad language-reasoning ambition into a deployable representation-learning mechanism and explicitly qualify emergent reasoning claims.
research_lesson: Show both offline prediction and closed-loop behavior, while distinguishing learned useful signals from demonstrated reasoning.
reviewer_question: How are train/test trajectories separated, how reliable are text labels, and what is the effect of excluded scenarios and the operational collision definition?

evidence_pages.observation: The All column includes extra unlabeled samples rather than averaging scenario columns.
A human yielding to the robot counts as collision; evaluation is small-scale feasibility.
Narrow-passage success is only 4/10; authors require further tests before asserting emergent reasoning.

limits_or_counterexample: Text removal leaves FDE unchanged in Table III. Latent alignment and attention maps do not establish human-like reasoning or safe general deployment.
citation: Amirreza Payandeh, Anuj Pokhrel, Daeun Song, Marcos Zampieri, and Xuesu Xiao . Narrate2Nav: Real-Time Visual Navigation with Implicit Language Reasoning in Human-Centric Environments . Accepted by 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA).

title: Adaptive Dynamics Planning for Robot Navigation
reading_depth: Main text read in full, including extraction-order text following reference heading; references not close-read
problem: Fixed dynamics-fidelity schedules allocate computation poorly as obstacle complexity changes.
mechanism: Train a TD3 meta-controller to choose rollout temporal-resolution parameters within classical planners and a recovery-enabled navigation system.
evidence_scope: 225 held-out BARN worlds, hardest-world subset, fifty unpublished challenge worlds, and two physical courses with eight total runs per method.
writing_move: Name the prior method's restrictive assumption, preserve its core machinery, and compare augmented versus unaugmented planner pairs.
research_lesson: Test a general augmentation across multiple hosts and report how failure modes change, not just the final aggregate score.
reviewer_question: What are the untrimmed success/collision distributions, and does excluding the five best and worst of twenty runs conceal rare catastrophic failures?

evidence_pages.observation: Planners and recovery-enabled systems are explicitly distinguished.
Evaluation discards half the trials; MPPI adaptation trades fewer collisions for more timeouts.
Both standalone systems succeed 8/8; ADP's physical advantage there is time, not success rate.

limits_or_counterexample: Greater training-environment count is not monotonically better; small physical samples and trimmed simulation statistics cannot establish rare-failure safety.
citation: Yuanjie Lu, Mingyang Mao, Tong Xu, Linji Wang, Xiaomin Lin, and Xuesu Xiao . Adaptive Dynamics Planning for Robot Navigation . Accepted by 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA).

title: Legs Over Arms: On the Predictive Value of Lower-Body Pose for Human Trajectory Prediction from Egocentric Robot Perception
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Point-mass pedestrian forecasts discard skeletal cues, but the most useful body regions and sensing requirements are unclear.
mechanism: Hold the HST forecasting backbone fixed while varying full-, upper-, lower-body 2D/3D keypoints and derived gait cues.
evidence_scope: Controlled feature comparisons on JRDB and three hours of panoramic social-navigation data, predicting four seconds from two seconds of history.
writing_move: Frame a feature-selection study as an answerable empirical question rather than forcing a new architecture contribution.
research_lesson: Control architecture and feature availability, then translate results into sensing implications with explicit limits.
reviewer_question: Do lower-body gains persist across backbones, pose quality, occlusion patterns, and closed-loop navigation rather than only best-of-mode forecast error?

evidence_pages.observation: Metrics include minimum-mode, most-likely, and probabilistic errors; evaluation requires partial pose availability.
Full 2D pose slightly exceeds lower-body-only pose on the new dataset; authors note backbone dependence.

limits_or_counterexample: The title's lower-body advantage is strongest for 3D JRDB features, not universal for 2D panoramic inputs. Sensor-placement explanation is plausible but not independently isolated.
citation: Nhat Le, Daeun Song, and Xuesu Xiao . Legs Over Arms: On the Predictive Value of Lower-Body Pose for Human Trajectory Prediction from Egocentric Robot Perception . Accepted by 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA).

title: Failing Gracefully: Mitigating Impact of Inevitable Robot Failures
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Preventing task failure does not capture harm when unavoidable malfunctions occur.
mechanism: Separate conditional interaction likelihood from severity; combine estimated failure impact with motion cost, supported by a MuJoCo failure-injection benchmark.
evidence_scope: Four precomputed Panda pick-and-place trajectories, sixty simulations each, with 25% drop probability; broader fault types are infrastructure rather than all experimentally validated scenarios.
writing_move: Change the research question from whether failure happens to what failure harms, then provide a measurable formulation and tool.
research_lesson: Distinguish a risk-assessment framework from an implemented optimizer and validate proxy predictions against observed consequences.
reviewer_question: Is geometric overlap a calibrated interaction probability, and do predicted and observed costs share scale and failure conditioning?

evidence_pages.observation: The objective conditions on failure rather than modeling its probability.
Predicted safety costs around 0.35–0.43 correspond to observed costs 3.33 and 5.6 for two trajectories.
Integration into practical planning and learned probability models are future work.

limits_or_counterexample: Failure ranking and magnitude are imperfect; severity is predefined and complete environmental knowledge assumed. Contact proxies do not establish human injury risk.
citation: Duc M. Nguyen, Saad A. Ghani, Andrew Marshall, Allison Andreyev, Gregory J. Stein, and Xuesu Xiao . Failing Gracefully: Mitigating Impact of Inevitable Robot Failures . Accepted by 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA).
venue_full: Accepted by 2026 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)

title: E-SocialNav: Efficient Socially Compliant Navigation with Language Models
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Large language models can be slow and poorly aligned with socially appropriate navigation under limited task-specific data.
mechanism: Train a small multimodal model with projector-only supervised tuning, then LoRA preference optimization on human answers versus locally corrupted alternatives.
evidence_scope: 265 training and sixty test images derived from SNEI; model/vision-tower combinations, text similarity, exact action accuracy, and inference throughput comparisons.
writing_move: Make efficiency and small-data specialization coequal objectives, with a staged trainable/frozen-component diagram.
research_lesson: Match the claim to the measured layer: better annotated action text is evidence about decision generation, not physical social-navigation success.
reviewer_question: Are correlated video frames split safely, preference negatives realistic, and social norms assessed beyond agreement with one annotation standard?

evidence_pages.observation: Different components train in each stage.
Final action accuracy is 0.550 and throughput 2.354 FPS.
Evaluation uses a sixty-sample random test split; subjective user studies remain future work.

limits_or_counterexample: No closed-loop physical evaluation is reported. Energy reduction is motivated by compactness, not directly measured, and annotation disagreement need not imply unsafe behavior.
citation: Ling Xiao, Daeun Song, Xuesu Xiao , and Toshihiko Yamasaki. E-SocialNav: Efficient Socially Compliant Navigation with Language Models . 2026 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing (ICASSP).

title: Designing Multi-Robot Ground Video Sensemaking with Public Safety Professionals
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references on 19–22 not close-read
problem: Additional robot video can increase cognitive workload unless tools fit practitioners' verification, coordination, and accountability needs.
mechanism: Derive event taxonomy and design requirements with practitioners, construct scripted patrol videos, and link AI event proposals to clips, timelines, maps, search, and team notes.
evidence_scope: Five formative and nine summative professionals; twenty prerecorded videos/470 minutes; detector benchmark and qualitative task-based expert interviews, not a controlled workload trial.
writing_move: Maintain traceability from observed workflow pain to design requirement, interface feature, and evaluation question.
research_lesson: A sociotechnical contribution can be the task definition and evidence workflow, with model scores only one part of validation.
reviewer_question: Do self-reported efficiency and higher recall outweigh false-alarm verification cost, and whose community interests are absent from practitioner-centered design?

evidence_pages.observation: Sequential single-robot patrol recordings emulate simultaneous multi-robot coverage.
Overall recall improves but precision falls to 0.473 from Gemini's 0.696.
Discusses over-policing feedback, contestability, privacy, and staged-event limits.

limits_or_counterexample: Model-stated confidence is not demonstrated calibrated reliability. Interviews cannot establish causal workload reduction; event categories are local, not universal judgments of suspicious behavior.
citation: Puqi Zhou, Ali Asgarov, Aafiya Hussain, Wonjoon Park, Amit Paudyal, Sameep Shrestha, Chia-Wei Tang, Michael Lighthiser, Michael Hieb, Xuesu Xiao , Chris Thomas, and Sungsoo Ray Hong. Designing Multi-Robot Ground Video Sensemaking with Public Safety Professionals . 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems.

title: Verti-Arena: A Controllable and Standardized Indoor Testbed for Multi-Terrain Off-Road Autonomy
reading_depth: Main text read in full, including conclusion after reference heading; references not close-read
problem: Outdoor terrain lacks repeatability and precise ground truth; simulation simplifies important contact dynamics.
mechanism: Create an 8×8 m reconfigurable indoor arena with ten blended material categories, elevation differences, synchronized onboard sensing, and motion capture.
evidence_scope: Data/platform description plus cross-zone dynamics prediction on five representative terrains, comparing zone-specific MLPs and classical kinematic models.
writing_move: Justify a physical research resource by the experimental controls it unlocks, then demonstrate that its terrain variation matters to a downstream model.
research_lesson: Benchmark value includes controllability, measurement quality, and meaningful distribution shifts, not just physical scale or visual diversity.
reviewer_question: Are terrain reset procedures, train/test trajectory independence, remote-access operation, and material variation specified reproducibly?

evidence_pages.observation: Materials are blended and reconfigurable rather than isolated tiles.
Forward models deliberately omit environmental features to reveal zone dependence.
Small stone-dust area narrows sampled states, so low prediction error need not mean easy terrain.

limits_or_counterexample: Results use low gear and locked differentials; apparent difficulty ranking partly reflects collection geometry and behavior, not intrinsic surface difficulty.
citation: Haiyue Chen, Aniket Datar, Tong Xu, Francesco Cancelliere, Harsh Rangwala, Madhan Balaji Rao, Daeun Song, David Eichinger, and Xuesu Xiao . title: Dom, cars don't fly!---Or do they? In-Air Vehicle Maneuver for High-Speed Off-Road Navigation
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Airborne ground vehicles must prepare landing attitude within a fixed short time, despite limited actuation.
mechanism: Use wheel inertia and steering-induced gyroscopic effects, learn angular acceleration, integrate through physics, and plan against a shrinking time-to-landing horizon with actuator limits.
evidence_scope: One hour of gimbal data; four indoor control tests against PID; seven outdoor ramp launches, with manual approach steering and no outdoor PID comparison for safety.
writing_move: Use a memorable capability question, then immediately identify physical controllability and the unusual terminal-time constraint.
research_lesson: Study dangerous capability in a controlled apparatus first, while clearly separating apparatus comparisons from outdoor demonstrations.
reviewer_question: How do gimbal inertia, landing-time uncertainty, and state-dependent saturation affect transfer, and which attitude axes are actually controllable?

evidence_pages.observation: The method explicitly lacks direct yaw-acceleration control.
Learned acceleration is composed with deterministic integration; horizon ends at landing.
Outdoor control begins after takeoff; complete off-road integration remains future work.

limits_or_counterexample: Conclusion language about yaw maneuvering exceeds the stated direct-control mechanism. Outdoor trials establish feasibility, not comparative superiority or autonomous takeoff-to-landing reliability.
citation: Anuj Pokhrel, Aniket Datar, and Xuesu Xiao . Dom, cars don't fly!---Or do they? In-Air Vehicle Maneuver for High-Speed Off-Road Navigation . 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).
venue_full: 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)

title: Reward Training Wheels: Adaptive Auxiliary Rewards for Robotics Reinforcement Learning
reading_depth: Main text read in full; physical PDF page 5 visually inspected for Tables II/III
problem: Fixed auxiliary rewards may assist early learning but bias later behavior away from the primary task.
mechanism: A teacher observes histories of weights and reward signals, adapts auxiliary weights, and learns against the student's primary reward while the student learns control.
evidence_scope: Two simulated tasks compare expert weights, random weights, and MPPI; five physical off-road trials per learned policy; learning curves and weight evolution.
writing_move: Use the training-wheels analogy to explain changing assistance, then formalize separate student and teacher objectives.
research_lesson: Preserve the task objective while adapting assistance, and use randomization as a baseline for whether adaptation is informative.
reviewer_question: Are gains robust across seeds, teacher compute, fixed-weight tuning budgets, and primary-only baselines, and are reported improvements relative percentages or percentage points?

evidence_pages.observation: Teacher reward is the student's primary reward.
82.67−80.32=2.35 percentage points, approximately 2.93% relative; off-road 76.67 versus 34.44 is 122.62% relative.
Physical success is RTW 5/5, ER 2/5, RR 1/5.

limits_or_counterexample: Off-road roll/pitch do not uniformly improve in simulation. Correlated weight trajectories suggest but do not prove discovered functional relationships; five physical successes do not establish general reliability.
citation: Linji Wang, Tong Xu, Yuanjie Lu, and Xuesu Xiao . Reward Training Wheels: Adaptive Auxiliary Rewards for Robotics Reinforcement Learning . 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).
venue_full: 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)

title: Decremental Dynamics Planning for Robot Navigation
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Abruptly changing from a dynamics-free global plan to a dynamics-aware local plan creates inconsistency, while full-fidelity long-horizon planning is expensive.
mechanism: Allocate finer integration and denser collision checks near the robot, reducing fidelity farther into the horizon; augment several existing planners and build a standalone system with recovery modes.
evidence_scope: Three repetitions across 300 BARN worlds at three speeds; harder-world subsets and competition results; ten physical runs per tested system.
writing_move: Turn a familiar architectural discontinuity into a continuous design variable, then demonstrate compatibility with multiple planner families.
research_lesson: Separate an algorithmic ingredient from a deployable system containing additional braking and recovery logic.
reviewer_question: How much improvement comes from integration scheduling, collision-check density, and recovery modes under matched compute budgets?

evidence_pages.observation: Fidelity scheduling changes time integration and boundary sampling.
Standalone planner contains additional mode switching.
Physical standalone DDP succeeds 10/10, but the comparison involves complete systems.

limits_or_counterexample: Higher success can cost time. Simulation-ranking language is inconsistent between reported scores and conclusion; verify competition placement before reuse. Far-horizon approximation is not a formal safety guarantee.
citation: Yuanjie Lu, Tong Xu, Linji Wang, Nick Hawes, and Xuesu Xiao . Decremental Dynamics Planning for Robot Navigation . 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).

title: AutoSpatial: Visual-Language Reasoning for Social Robot Navigation through Efficient Spatial Reasoning Learning
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Generic VLMs describe people with ambiguous spatial language and weak robot-relative reasoning; detailed manual annotation is expensive.
mechanism: Define robot-frame position, distance, and motion categories, automatically label individual pedestrians, then combine these labels with a small manually annotated scene-level conversation dataset.
evidence_scope: CODA train/test spatial prediction, scene-level questions assessed by several VLM judges, and seven graduate-student evaluators on 49 scenarios; no closed-loop navigation trial.
writing_move: Make language grounding concrete with discretized definitions before explaining a two-stage annotation/training pipeline.
research_lesson: Spend human annotation effort on ambiguous interactions while automating well-specified geometric labels.
reviewer_question: Are correlated video frames separated across train/test, are labels independent of evaluation rules, and do better explanations improve executed navigation?

evidence_pages.observation: Five horizontal zones, five distance categories, and robot-frame motion directions reduce linguistic ambiguity.
Scene-level manual data comprise 72 examples; automated data provide much larger individual coverage.
Qualitative failures include gaze/body interpretation and camera-relative phrasing.

limits_or_counterexample: Multi-model judging is not an independent behavioral safety test; its 'cross-validation' is cross-model scoring rather than k-fold generalization.
citation: Yangzhe Kong, Daeun Song, Jing Liang, Dinesh Manocha, Ziyu Yao, and Xuesu Xiao . AutoSpatial: Visual-Language Reasoning for Social Robot Navigation through Efficient Spatial Reasoning Learning . 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).

title: T-CBF: Traversability-based Control Barrier Function to Navigate Vertically Challenging Terrain
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Collision avoidance alone does not prevent rollover or immobilization on vertically challenging terrain.
mechanism: Learn a terrain-and-control conditioned barrier from safe/unsafe physical samples and use it to constrain model-based trajectory planning.
evidence_scope: 4000 real samples, simulation on 30 Verti-Bench worlds, and 90 physical runs across three methods and three terrain difficulties.
writing_move: Extend the definition of safety to domain-specific failure modes, then connect labeled examples, certificate learning, and constrained planning.
research_lesson: State exactly what a success metric measures and distinguish empirical safe behavior from mathematical guarantees.
reviewer_question: Do the learned certificate and perception errors satisfy the assumptions needed for invariance, and is safe searching being confused with reaching the goal?

evidence_pages.observation: Safe/unsafe labels use attitude and low motion under commanded action.
Authors explicitly state validation is not formal proof under neural approximation and perception/localization errors.
Physical success means staying safe/mobile/searching, unlike goal-reaching simulation success.

limits_or_counterexample: The method trades traversal speed for safety. Thirty safe physical trials support the tested conditions, not universal safety, feasibility, or liveness.
citation: Manas Gupta and Xuesu Xiao . T-CBF: Traversability-based Control Barrier Function to Navigate Vertically Challenging Terrain . 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).

title: M2P2: A Multi-Modal Passive Perception Dataset for Off-Road Mobility in Extreme Low-Light Conditions
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Visible-light cameras fail in darkness while active sensing may violate a passive-perception requirement.
mechanism: Build a synchronized thermal/event/stereo sensor suite, common thermal checkerboard calibration, and 10.15-hour mobility dataset with active LiDAR reserved for ground truth.
evidence_scope: More than 32 km of collected data; thermal behavioral-cloning deployment on 3.6 km with 11 interventions; depth reconstruction and thermal-event odometry demonstrations.
writing_move: Organize a dataset contribution around the difficult measurement infrastructure and several downstream uses, not data volume alone.
research_lesson: Calibration, synchronization, missing-data accounting, and sensor replication are central scientific methods for multimodal research.
reviewer_question: Are training and route tests independent, are baseline modalities/domain adaptation matched, and does event subsampling faithfully reproduce actual darkness?

evidence_pages.observation: LiDAR synchronization triggers align cameras; GPS exists for 87.97% of the data.
Eleven interventions mainly address pavement/gravel thermal confusion.
Odometry uses one 157.5 m segment and artificially subsampled events.

limits_or_counterexample: A domain-trained thermal U-Net versus a large RGB-pretrained model establishes dataset utility, not architecture superiority. Navigation is assisted, and broad adverse-weather resilience is not experimentally established.
citation: Aniket Datar, Anuj Pokhrel, Mohammad Nazeri, Madhan B. Rao, Harsh Rangwala, Chenhui Pan, Yufan Zhang, Andre Harrison, Maggie Wigness, Philip R. Osteen, Jinwei Ye, and Xuesu Xiao . M2P2: A Multi-Modal Passive Perception Dataset for Off-Road Mobility in Extreme Low-Light Conditions . 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).

title: GACL: Grounded Adaptive Curriculum Learning with Active Task and Performance Monitoring
reading_depth: Main text read in full, including final-page figure captions; references not close-read
problem: Automatically generated curricula can drift from deployment-relevant tasks and ignore evolving student capability.
mechanism: Use a pretrained VAE task space, a regret-maximizing teacher with task/performance observations, and probabilistic interleaving of reference tasks with generated tasks.
evidence_scope: Two simulated domains, comparisons with no curriculum/manual curriculum/CLUTR, component-removal studies, and curriculum progression visualizations.
writing_move: Introduce three specific deficiencies and preserve the same three-part organization through mechanism and ablations.
research_lesson: Test both task acquisition and relevance of the training distribution; show what an adaptive generator actually produces over time.
reviewer_question: Do reference tasks represent truly independent target distributions, are training budgets matched, and are improvement/error-bar denominators and random-seed counts specified?

evidence_pages.observation: Alternating sampling is the grounding mechanism, not a learned guarantee of distribution match.
Target domains are procedurally generated simulations; implemented teacher history is only the latest task/reward.
Removing grounding gives the largest reported component drop.

limits_or_counterexample: General formal history differs from the one-step implementation. Ablations support contributions within this setup but do not establish that each component is universally essential or prove physical deployment benefit.
citation: Linji Wang, Zifan Xu, Peter Stone, and Xuesu Xiao . GACL: Grounded Adaptive Curriculum Learning with Active Task and Performance Monitoring . 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).

title: VertiSelector: Automatic Curriculum Learning for Wheeled Mobility on Vertically Challenging Terrain
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Random or manually scheduled rough-terrain training wastes samples and can generalize poorly.
mechanism: Prioritize terrain by absolute generalized-advantage estimates while mixing in staleness-based revisits; generate terrain by interpolating between flat and recorded rugged elevation maps.
evidence_scope: Three-run learning curves,50 simulated evaluation trials, ten physical trials per difficulty for VS/manual curriculum, and an outdoor demonstration.
writing_move: Explain an intuitive learning-potential hypothesis, then expose its exact score and revisit rule.
research_lesson: Pair curriculum-learning curves with harder held-out conditions and physical transfer, while retaining subgroup results and scale assumptions.
reviewer_question: Can TD error reflect irreducible noise rather than useful learning, and does model selection on the test terrain contaminate the generalization estimate?

evidence_pages.observation: Terrain diversity is a linear interpolation family; sampling mixes scores and staleness.
Simulation success 32/50 versus 26/50; physical easy terrain favors manual 9/10 versusVS 8/10, but hard favorsVS 5/10 versus 0/10.
Limitations explicitly include full-scale simulation versus RC-car validation and fixed material properties.

limits_or_counterexample: Absolute advantage is a learning-potential proxy, not true value error. Physical benefits are uneven by difficulty, and the best-model/test-terrain evaluation needs selection-protocol scrutiny.
citation: Tong Xu, Chenhui Pan, and Xuesu Xiao . VertiSelector: Automatic Curriculum Learning for Wheeled Mobility on Vertically Challenging Terrain . 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).

title: Dyna-LfLH: Learning Agile Navigation in Dynamic Environments from Learned Hallucination
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Expert demonstrations and risky exploration are expensive for dense dynamic-obstacle navigation.
mechanism: Invert planning: learn distributions of moving obstacles that explain existing easy-space trajectories, render scan histories, and train a local policy from synthetic scene/action pairs.
evidence_scope: Under ten minutes of open-space experience versus 8.7-hour expert behavior cloning;180 simulation trials per method and 20 physical trials each for three selected planners.
writing_move: Generalize an established paradigm by identifying its static-world assumption, then formalize the time-dependent inverse problem.
research_lesson: Data synthesis should preserve a task-relevant relationship, here approximately optimal motion under generated constraints.
reviewer_question: Does reconstructed-plan similarity ensure near-optimality and broad obstacle coverage, and how much benefit comes from history length or recovery safeguards?

evidence_pages.observation: Hallucinated obstacles have fixed velocities and independent Gaussian parameters.
Recovery is disabled in simulation; best success is only about 27%.
Physical success 50% versus 40% is 25% relative; recovery is enabled and obstacles are slower; mode collapse is acknowledged.

limits_or_counterexample: Physical and simulated success cannot be directly compared as task difficulty and safeguards differ. More synthetic data does not imply broad distributional coverage.
citation: Saad Abdul Ghani, Zizhao Wang, Peter Stone, and Xuesu Xiao . Dyna-LfLH: Learning Agile Navigation in Dynamic Environments from Learned Hallucination . 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).
venue_full: 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)

title: Social-LLaVA: Enhancing Robot Navigation through Human-Language Reasoning in Social Spaces
reading_depth: Main text read in full; physical PDF page 5 Table III visually verified
problem: Generic vision-language models lack the nuanced social context needed for human-facing robot navigation.
mechanism: Construct SNEI categorical and free-form human annotations, then fine-tune LLaVA to describe perception, prediction, reasoning, high-level action, and explanation.
evidence_scope: Over 40K VQA pairs from 2K SCAND scenes; categorical assessment and 15 human judges on 50 tasks; a hard-coded action-mapping proof of concept.
writing_move: Explicitly frame the dataset, rather than architectural novelty, as the primary contribution and pair structured evaluation with human interpretation.
research_lesson: Report distinct evaluation channels separately: persuasive explanations and accurate spatial predictions need not improve together.
reviewer_question: How are rater agreement, labeler dependence, split leakage, and action grounding assessed, and is fluency being mistaken for executable social competence?

evidence_pages.observation: One person verifies all annotations; the model is a dataset-utility proof of concept.
Overall categorical similarity .29 trails .30/.32; intention .26 wins but position .36 trails .42/.43.
Human free-form ratings favor Social-LLaVA; language-to-action grounding remains an open problem.

limits_or_counterexample: Human-rated language superiority is not universal metric superiority or closed-loop safety evidence; annotations embody contestable interpretations of social behavior.
citation: Amirreza Payandeh, Daeun Song, Mohammad Nazeri, Jing Liang, Praneel Mukherjee, Amir Hossain Raj, Yangzhe Kong, Dinesh Manocha, and Xuesu Xiao . title: Human-Robot Co-Transportation using Disturbance-Aware MPC with Pose Optimization
reading_depth: Main text and displayed derivation read; external supplement not read or independently proved
problem: Human trajectory uncertainty and mobile-manipulator redundancy interact, making otherwise adequate poses expensive to control.
mechanism: Evaluate sampled redundant arm/base poses using finite-horizon disturbance-aware Riccati recursions, then select the pose with lowest predicted tracking, control, and reconfiguration cost.
evidence_scope: Gaussian-disturbance simulations over 100 trials per setting, known versus predicted trajectories, periodic pose updates, computation timing, and Fetch trajectory-replay feasibility demonstrations.
writing_move: Derive a non-obvious mechanism: zero-mean uncertainty affects expected cost and pose selection even when it does not directly change the fixed-pose control law.
research_lesson: Explain exactly where an uncertainty model enters a decision instead of simply calling the whole controller uncertainty-aware.
reviewer_question: How robust is candidate selection to covariance misspecification, fixed-Jacobian approximation, joint constraints, and limited onboard parallelism?

evidence_pages.observation: Nominal trajectory and covariance are assumed known; orientation disturbance is excluded.
The covariance contribution enters the cost term governing pose choice.
Physical tests reproduce simulated trajectories; sample-based pose search is not global optimization.

limits_or_counterexample: Expected quadratic control cost is not measured energy, ergonomic benefit, or collision safety. Hardware replay is narrower than live human co-transportation validation.
citation: Al Jaber Mahmud, Amir Hossain Raj, Duc M. Nguyen, Xuesu Xiao , and Xuan Wang. Human-Robot Co-Transportation using Disturbance-Aware MPC with Pose Optimization . 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).
venue_full: 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)

title: Multi-Robot Coordination in an Adversarial Graph-Traversal Game
reading_depth: Main text and proofs read for argument/assumptions; no independent proof replication
problem: A shortest path through a changing graph ignores an adversary that reacts to the robot team's choices.
mechanism: Formulate a zero-sum stochastic game with team movement and bounded graph-changing actions; compute mixed equilibria, cheaper security bounds, and layered value iteration.
evidence_scope: Analytical security/goal-reaching results under explicit assumptions; illustrative graphs, road-network example, and randomly generated small graph experiments.
writing_move: Use minimal examples to isolate why mixing, backtracking, splitting, and synchronized traversal arise from the model.
research_lesson: When introducing discounting for computational tractability, separately prove that the surrogate objective still achieves the original termination goal.
reviewer_question: Do the reachability, positive-cost, information, and discount assumptions hold, and how does joint-state complexity scale beyond the small examples?

evidence_pages.observation: Goal is reachable from every node, non-goal costs are positive, and both players observe the full modeled state.
A discount-factor condition ensures almost-sure goal reaching under equilibrium policies.
Synchronized risky-edge traversal prevents the adversary from penalizing both separated robots.

limits_or_counterexample: Graph costs are risk proxies, not physical robot dynamics. Limited perception and incomplete knowledge are explicitly deferred to future work.
citation: James Berneburg, Xuan Wang, Xuesu Xiao , and Daigo Shishika. Multi-Robot Coordination in an Adversarial Graph-Traversal Game . 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).
venue_full: 2025 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)

title: MOSU: Autonomous Long-range Robot Navigation with Multi-modal Scene Understanding
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Coarse public routing cannot resolve local geometry, terrain semantics, and social context.
mechanism: Combine coarse GPS waypoints, LiDAR-conditioned candidate trajectories, image segmentation, VLM ranking, and reactive DWA execution with two speed modes.
evidence_scope: GND-based trajectory traversability/target-distance comparison, inference times, qualitative scene examples, and a system description; long-range closed-loop trial counts are not established in the reported table.
writing_move: Assign each sensor/model an interpretable role and show failure examples motivating complementary information.
research_lesson: Make module outputs and fusion weights explicit, then evaluate both local predictive quality and the whole deployed task.
reviewer_question: What happens when geometric, semantic, and language scores disagree, when VLM output is stale, or when coarse GPS points cross an unsafe region?

evidence_pages.observation: Waypoints are about 50 m apart with 10 m proximity updates.
Final trajectory maximizes a weighted sum of geometry, semantics, language rank, and goal progress.
Traversability 77% versus best baseline 70% is 10% relative, with 2.30 s inference; small cliffs remain problematic.

limits_or_counterexample: Trajectory-waypoint traversability is not route completion or traffic safety. Broad 'comprehensive understanding' claims require more than complementary modules and qualitative social examples.
citation: Jing Liang, Kasun Weerakoon, Daeun Song, Senthurbavan Kirubaharan, Xuesu Xiao , and Dinesh Manocha. MOSU: Autonomous Long-range Robot Navigation with Multi-modal Scene Understanding . Accepted by 19th International Symposium on Experimental Robotics (ISER 2025).

title: Verti-Bench: A General and Scalable Off-Road Mobility Benchmark for Vertically Challenging Terrain
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Static datasets cannot evaluate the states caused by a new navigation policy, and bespoke robot/testbed choices prevent fair mobility comparisons.
mechanism: Standardize interactive Chrono environments across geometry, material properties, obstacle distributions, and vehicle scales, with reusable tasks, metrics, data, and interfaces.
evidence_scope: Ten systems on 1000 tasks each, plus 30 physical trials for three representative systems across two elevations.
writing_move: Explain why an existing evaluation paradigm is structurally insufficient before introducing benchmark dimensions and diagnostic failure categories.
research_lesson: Benchmark design should expose failures and reverse assumptions, not merely rank a favored method.
reviewer_question: Which real-world phenomena are abstracted away, do baselines receive comparable training, and does simulation ranking survive perception noise and physical distribution shifts?

evidence_pages.observation: Physics fidelity is prioritized over photorealism and training speed.
Success allows obstacle contact and means reaching within 10 m in 60 s.
Ground-truth perception is supplied; none of the evaluated systems is trained in Verti-Bench; manual curriculum beats automatic curriculum.
Simple PID can be fastest and competitive on low elevation; traversal times condition on success.

limits_or_counterexample: A mobility benchmark is not a complete perception-and-control safety benchmark. Many simulation trials cannot eliminate model bias or substitute for representative physical testing.
citation: Tong Xu, Chenhui Pan, Madhan B. Rao, Aniket Datar, Anuj Pokhrel, Yuanjie Lu, Xuesu Xiao . Verti-Bench: A General and Scalable Off-Road Mobility Benchmark for Vertically Challenging Terrain . Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) 2025.

title: VertiCoder: Self-Supervised Kinodynamic Representation Learning on Vertically Challenging Terrain
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Task-specific terrain models overfit and require repeated representation learning for related mobility tasks.
mechanism: Mask historical terrain, action, and pose tokens and predict the next patch; reuse the context token through frozen or fine-tuned heads for dynamics, control, and reconstruction.
evidence_scope: One-hour dataset with 9:1 split, four offline downstream tasks, separate masking/token-order ablations, and ten physical BC trials per model.
writing_move: Make representation reuse tangible through multiple downstream equations, parameter counts, and frozen-versus-fine-tuned comparisons.
research_lesson: A shared representation needs both transfer tests and a deployed-task check; pretext reconstruction should not be counted as wholly independent transfer.
reviewer_question: Are temporal split leakage, pretraining compute, history differences, and total versus learnable parameter counts controlled consistently?

evidence_pages.observation: Patch reconstruction is also the pretraining task; dataset includes planar and rocky driving.
Physical BC succeeds 8/10 versus 7/10 but is slower; authors report a gap to specialized TAL/WMVCT planners.
Local context omits global terrain information and slow motion yields near-duplicate patches.

limits_or_counterexample: Offline generalization does not establish parity with specialized deployed planners. Body text and table use inconsistent encoder parameter totals, so audit efficiency claims before copying them.
citation: Mohammad Nazeri, Aniket Datar, Anuj Pokhrel, Chenhui Pan, Garrett Warnell, and Xuesu Xiao . VertiCoder: Self-Supervised Kinodynamic Representation Learning on Vertically Challenging Terrain . 2025 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA).
venue_full: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
