title: Multi-Goal Motion Memory
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Repeated multi-goal planning wastes prior solutions and must jointly handle route ordering, obstacles, and dynamics.
mechanism: Retrieve learned goal-pair trajectories, repair them through collision-checked roadmap sampling, estimate travel costs for tour selection, and guide motion-tree expansion with random fallback.
evidence_scope: Four simulated environment families, two robot models,4/9/16 fixed goals,400 instances per setting, and timing plus path-length comparisons.
writing_move: Map the contribution to three existing pipeline stages and explain how inaccurate predictions are corrected instead of requiring perfect learning.
research_lesson: Use learned outputs to guide a verifiable search, and measure solution quality alongside speed.
reviewer_question: Are goal-pair training/storage and preprocessing costs amortized honestly, do fallback rules preserve feasibility, and what happens to failures and latency tails?

evidence_pages.observation: Separate goal-pair representations assume a fixed goal set.
Runtime statistics discard the lowest and highest 25% of instances, retaining only the middle half.
Car-trained memory transfers to a simulated snake-like model; SequentialRRT is omitted from path-quality comparisons due to frequent failure.

limits_or_counterexample: Trimmed runtime cannot characterize worst-case real-time behavior. Fixed-goal simulation transfer does not establish arbitrary-goal or physical generalization.
citation: Yuanjie Lu, Dibyendu Das, Erion Plaku, and Xuesu Xiao . Multi-Goal Motion Memory . 2025 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA).
venue_full: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
research_line: Motion memory / experience reuse in planning

title: GND: Global Navigation Dataset with Multi-Modal Perception and Multi-Category Traversability in Outdoor Campus Environments
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Long-range outdoor navigation requires geometric and semantic traversability that differs across robot capabilities.
mechanism: Collect multi-sensor campus routes, register maps, annotate five terrain categories, and demonstrate capability-conditioned planning, trajectory generation, and 360-degree place recognition.
evidence_scope: 53 km,668 minutes, ten campuses, approximately 2.7 km² coverage; applications are illustrative rather than a complete standardized navigation benchmark.
writing_move: Name two distinctive resource dimensions—global scale and multi-category traversability—and organize downstream demonstrations around them.
research_lesson: A dataset should include an extensible processing pipeline and concrete use cases, while acknowledging that evaluation protocols are a separate deliverable.
reviewer_question: Are semantic labels, annotation agreement, map registration error, dataset splits, and different robot-capability assumptions reproducibly specified?

evidence_pages.observation: Standardized processing uses odometry, map registration, and a single campus coordinate frame.
Traversal categories depend on the robot rather than a universal free/obstacle split.
Authors explicitly identify benchmark scenarios and metrics as unfinished work.

limits_or_counterexample: Roadway suitability cannot follow from robot speed alone; dynamic traffic rules and risk require separate treatment. Campus coverage and illustrative applications do not establish global-navigation reliability.
citation: Jing Liang, Dibyendu Das, Daeun Song, Md Nahid Hasan Shuvo, Mohammad Durrani, Karthik Taranath, Ivan Penskiy, Dinesh Manocha, and Xuesu Xiao . GND: Global Navigation Dataset with Multi-Modal Perception and Multi-Category Traversability in Outdoor Campus Environments . 2025 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA).
venue_full: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
research_line: Social navigation: data, benchmarks, and language reasoning

title: Reinforcement Learning for Wheeled Mobility on Vertically Challenging Terrain
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Complex wheel-terrain interaction makes online high-fidelity modeling and planning difficult on small robots.
mechanism: Build a Chrono terrain simulator from physical elevation data, interpolate terrain difficulty, and train a PPO policy using compressed maps and progress/stability rewards.
evidence_scope: Four simulated terrain stages with 25 trials each against two heuristic baselines; qualitative physical V4W demonstrations.
writing_move: Present an enabling simulator, learning formulation, and feasibility demonstration as a first step toward a broader capability.
research_lesson: Connect physical platform capability to an experimentally accessible learning problem, then turn manual curriculum limitations into follow-up research.
reviewer_question: Does curriculum beat matched random terrain training, how much does SWAE contribute, and are transfer success rates measured across unseen physical terrain?

evidence_pages.observation: Recorded rock geometry anchors simulation generation.
Policy predicts speed/steering targets tracked by PID; hand-designed reward terms remain essential.
All methods succeed on easy stages; RL15/25 beats heuristics 10/25 and 12/25 on hardest stage.

limits_or_counterexample: Physical evidence is a demonstration, not a repeated comparative trial. Calling the method end-to-end does not mean it eliminates the encoder, reward design, terrain generation, or low-level controller.
citation: Tong Xu, Chenhui Pan, and Xuesu Xiao . Reinforcement Learning for Wheeled Mobility on Vertically Challenging Terrain . 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Safety, Security, and Rescue Robotics (SSRR).
venue_full: 2024 IEEE International Symposium on Safety, Security, and Rescue Robotics (SSRR)
research_line: Verti: wheeled mobility on vertically challenging terrain

title: Multi-Strategy Deployment-Time Learning and Adaptation for Navigation under Uncertainty
reading_depth: Main text and included technical appendix read in full; references not close-read
problem: Early poor performance can cause a selector to ignore policies that later improve through deployment-time learning.
mechanism: Replay updated policies counterfactually on prior navigation records to refresh cost bounds, then constrain bandit-like selection among static, visually adapted, and newly learned policies.
evidence_scope: Three simulated maze cue distributions,50-trial deployments, selection baselines, strategy-removal studies, and computational accounting.
writing_move: Make the nonstationarity failure concrete, then design environments that distinguish appearance changes from changed task semantics.
research_lesson: Evaluate adaptation only when it is actually useful; successful visual translation need not restore the decision-relevant relationship.
reviewer_question: Are counterfactual bounds valid for the chosen planner, is replay evaluation independent of training data, and is offline compute compatible with deployment duty cycles?

evidence_pages.observation: Five-fold validation addresses reuse of deployment data; models update every ten trials.
Replay folds exclude the data used to fit their respective policies.
An identity visual mapping fails to fix reversed goal cues.
CycleGAN training takes about 3 h, versus 20 s for one policy/trial replay.

limits_or_counterexample: Idle-time compute and model-based counterfactual compatibility are substantial assumptions. Asymptotic guarantees presume eventual policy convergence, not arbitrary ongoing nonstationarity.
citation: Abhishek Paudel, Xuesu Xiao , and Gregory J. Stein. Multi-Strategy Deployment-Time Learning and Adaptation for Navigation under Uncertainty . 2024 Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL).
venue_full: 2024 Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL)

title: Terrain-Attentive Learning for Efficient 6-DoF Kinodynamic Modeling on Vertically Challenging Terrain
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Terrain-conditioned 6-DoF rollouts require costly repeated map cropping and sequential state prediction.
mechanism: Pretrain a full-map representation with pose-conditioned patch reconstruction; encode the map once per planning cycle and query smaller attention/dynamics components for each transition.
evidence_scope: One hour of physical data, one-step and long-horizon model prediction, and ten robot trials per planner on rearranged rocky terrain.
writing_move: Explain the computation bottleneck at the level of repeated operations, then directly connect representation design to amortized execution.
research_lesson: Measure the downstream task even when the component metric improves dramatically, and report when the expected benefit does not materialize.
reviewer_question: Does prediction improvement survive matched planning frequency/compute, and what are the effects of temporal train/test overlap and omitted terrain semantics?

evidence_pages.observation: Sequential rollouts prevent pre-processing all future patches in parallel.
Reported average model-error reduction 51.1% still yields 10/10 success for both TAL andWMVCT.
Authors propose planning-frequency cost as an explanation for missing navigation improvement.

limits_or_counterexample: The latency explanation is a hypothesis, not isolated causal evidence. Better prediction accuracy is not automatically better closed-loop navigation, and geometry alone omits friction/deformation.
citation: Aniket Datar, Chenhui Pan, Mohammad Nazeri, Anuj Pokhrel, and Xuesu Xiao . Terrain-Attentive Learning for Efficient 6-DoF Kinodynamic Modeling on Vertically Challenging Terrain . 2024 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).
venue_full: 2024 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
research_line: Verti: wheeled mobility on vertically challenging terrain

title: VANP: Learning Where to See for Navigation with Self-Supervised Vision-Action Pre-Training
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Generic visual pretraining may emphasize salient objects rather than features relevant to navigation.
mechanism: Align embeddings of past images, future actions, and a future goal image using a non-contrastive VICReg objective; transfer the visual encoder to trajectory prediction.
evidence_scope: Curated SCAND/MuSoHu samples,8000 held-out samples, frozen/fine-tuned encoder comparisons, signal/augmentation ablations, activation visualizations, and an uncluttered physical proof of concept.
writing_move: Reverse a behavioral intuition—navigation decisions indicate relevant visual regions—into a measurable pretext task.
research_lesson: Compare representation quality under both freezing and fine-tuning; include the data conditions that cause representation collapse.
reviewer_question: Do activation maps establish feature necessity, are pretraining and downstream compute counted separately, and are correlated sequences split independently?

evidence_pages.observation: Pretraining lasts 200 epochs; downstream end-to-end training takes 100 versus 50 for transferred models.
Relative advantages depend on single/multi-frame and frozen/fine-tuned setting.
Near-unchanging sequences can collapse representations; physical tests are restricted for safety.

limits_or_counterexample: Half-training-time claims concern the downstream stage, not total pretraining expense. Heatmap agreement with intuition is interpretive evidence, not a causal explanation of safe behavior.
citation: Mohammad Nazeri, Junzhe Wang, Amirreza Payandeh, and Xuesu Xiao . VANP: Learning Where to See for Navigation with Self-Supervised Vision-Action Pre-Training . 2024 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).
venue_full: 2024 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
research_line: Social navigation: data, benchmarks, and language reasoning

title: Team Coordination on Graphs: Problem, Analysis, and Algorithms
reading_depth: Main text read in full, including proof sketch; mathematical claims not independently proved; references not close-read
problem: Conventional multi-robot routing often avoids interference but does not exploit support actions that lower teammates’ traversal risk/cost.
mechanism: Formalize supportive interactions on a graph; derive joint-state search, coordination-event enumeration, and receding-horizon optimistic coordination.
evidence_scope: Random graph families, teams of three to seven, 900 algorithm/problem trials, and targeted scaling/horizon experiments.
writing_move: Use problem structure to explain why different algorithm families scale with different parameters, rather than presenting one universally superior method.
research_lesson: Distinguish known optimality gaps from proxy comparisons when an exact solver cannot finish.
reviewer_question: Which assumptions make the guarantee hold, how often must support pairs repeat, and does polynomial scaling keep the number of support pairs fixed?

evidence_pages.observation: Support/waiting assumptions and a hardness proof sketch bound the formal problem.
Implemented event search allows each support pair once; its complexity depends factorially on support-event count.
TrueOptimality and NaiveOptimality have different denominators; some exact-solver points are absent.

limits_or_counterexample: Restricted event enumeration can lose optimality, and receding-horizon coordination is local. A good naïve-policy ratio is not a certified approximation to the global optimum.
citation: Yanlin Zhou, Manshi Limbu, Gregory J. Stein, Xuan Wang, Daigo Shishika, and Xuesu Xiao . Team Coordination on Graphs: Problem, Analysis, and Algorithms . 2024 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).
venue_full: 2024 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)

title: DTG : Diffusion-based Trajectory Generation for Mapless Global Navigation
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read; externally linked supplementary appendix not accessed
problem: Mapless local navigation struggles to propose traversable trajectories toward distant goals without a global map at deployment.
mechanism: A conditional recurrent diffusion model uses LiDAR history, velocity, and goal; progressive traversability training supplements imitation of map-derived A* trajectories.
evidence_scope: Held-out outdoor trajectory prediction, architecture/loss comparisons, and physical navigation with a local DWA controller; detailed external appendix is outside this reading.
writing_move: Position a compact recurrent denoiser as an explicit accuracy–latency compromise and separate global trajectory generation from local obstacle handling.
research_lesson: A mapless inference claim must disclose privileged map-based training and downstream collision-avoidance dependencies.
reviewer_question: How does the distance-ratio proxy relate to actual closed-loop route length, are sensor inputs matched across baselines, and is total planning latency measured?

evidence_pages.observation: Training trajectories use a full traversability map; smaller/dynamic obstacles are delegated to local planning.
Traversability loss is introduced progressively; physical generation operates with DWA.
CRNN inference is 0.13 s versus 2.09 s for U-Net, while its traversability score is slightly lower.

limits_or_counterexample: Offline distance-ratio improvement is not demonstrated equivalent to the same percentage of physical travel-distance reduction. A soft traversability loss is not a feasibility guarantee.
citation: Jing Liang, Amirreza Payandeh, Daeun Song, Xuesu Xiao , and Dinesh Manocha. DTG : Diffusion-based Trajectory Generation for Mapless Global Navigation . 2024 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).
venue_full: 2024 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
research_line: Social navigation: data, benchmarks, and language reasoning

title: Bi-CL: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Robots Coordination Through Bi-level Optimization
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Joint movement/support learning has a large action space, and globally optimized support actions may be impossible to reproduce from local observations.
mechanism: Let RL choose movement and an inner optimizer choose support; imitate support locally while an alignment penalty gradually makes the global optimizer’s actions more locally realizable.
evidence_scope: Abstract one-dimensional multi-robot/fire scenarios, alignment-coefficient comparisons, centralized/decentralized reward-gap measurements, and MADDPG/QMIX training comparisons.
writing_move: Turn a deployment mismatch into a named quantity—training reward versus true execution reward—before proposing its remedy.
research_lesson: Measure executable performance, not only a privileged training objective; tuning an alignment penalty can trade reward against information compatibility.
reviewer_question: Does support truly affect reward but not transitions, what is the inner oracle’s compute budget, and how does local execution degrade under noise or unseen team sizes?

evidence_pages.observation: Reduction assumes a transition independent of support and a directly solvable inner optimization.
RL-Reward, executed T-Reward, and their gap are defined separately.
Strong alignment can reduce the gap yet hurt return; coefficient 10 is often better than 50.

limits_or_counterexample: These are stylized simulations, not physical coordination evidence. Faster learning does not by itself establish lower wall-clock cost when an optimization oracle supplies supervision.
citation: Zechen Hu, Daigo Shishika, Xuesu Xiao , and Xuan Wang. Bi-CL: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Robots Coordination Through Bi-level Optimization . 2024 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).
venue_full: 2024 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)

title: Learning Coordinated Maneuver in Adversarial Environments
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: A team following risky routes must trade progress against slowing down to guard teammates.
mechanism: Hybrid PPO selects continuous movement and discrete guarding; interpolated one-hot position encoding and reward shaping support learning in a centralized abstract environment.
evidence_scope: Three one-dimensional hazard configurations, interpreted movement/guarding trajectories, a repositioned-hazard example, and comparisons with greedy behavior and time-limited numerical optimization.
writing_move: Use annotated behavior traces to make an otherwise opaque learned coordination policy understandable, then acknowledge uncertain global optimality.
research_lesson: Separate policy reuse after expensive offline learning from per-instance optimization; use behavior stories as explanations, not proofs.
reviewer_question: Are adversaries strategic or merely static hazards, do risk discounts correspond to physical protection, and what optimality/runtime claims survive matched total compute?

evidence_pages.observation: Risk is an assumed multiplicative guarding-discount model on fixed one-dimensional routes.
Hazard positions are randomized during training but static within a trial; behavior plots illustrate guard handoffs.
PPO is worse than BONMIN in one setting; authors acknowledge much longer offline training.

limits_or_counterexample: The title’s adversarial setting is not a demonstrated game against adaptive opponents. An optimizer’s timeout or failure to converge is not proof that the learned policy is globally optimal.
citation: Zechen Hu, Manshi Limbu, Daigo Shishika, Xuesu Xiao , and Xuan Wang. Learning Coordinated Maneuver in Adversarial Environments . 2024 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).
venue_full: 2024 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)

title: Toward Wheeled Mobility on Vertically Challenging Terrain: Platforms, Datasets, and Algorithms
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Treating all vertical protrusions as obstacles may underuse the mechanical mobility of conventional wheeled robots.
mechanism: Build two instrumented off-the-shelf crawler platforms, release first-person teleoperation datasets, and compare open-loop, rule-based, and behavior-cloned crawling controllers.
evidence_scope: 240 controlled physical trials across two platforms, three terrain difficulties, and four controller/training combinations, followed by qualitative outdoor demonstrations.
writing_move: Translate a provocative capability hypothesis into hardware desiderata, a reproducible testbed, and deliberately simple baseline algorithms.
research_lesson: Cross-platform transfer can reveal that a less capable embodiment elicits more informative demonstrations; test that explanation separately from dataset-size effects.
reviewer_question: Which hardware modifications are essential, do transfer gains survive matched demonstration quantity, and how are time-on-success and outdoor failures reported?

evidence_pages.observation: Seven hardware desiderata make the mechanical and sensing assumptions explicit.
All tested controllers keep low gear and locked differentials; BC uses only depth and two control outputs.
V6W benefits more from V4W demonstrations; difficult natural terrain remains a failure case.

limits_or_counterexample: The proposed full action/sensor formulation is broader than the evaluated controller. Cross-deployment supports a demonstration-quality hypothesis but does not isolate its cause; outdoor mobility is not quantitatively benchmarked.
citation: Aniket Datar, Chenhui Pan, Mohammad Nazeri, and Xuesu Xiao . Toward Wheeled Mobility on Vertically Challenging Terrain: Platforms, Datasets, and Algorithms . 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA).
venue_full: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
research_line: Verti: wheeled mobility on vertically challenging terrain

title: Motion Memory: Leveraging Past Experiences to Accelerate Future Motion Planning
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Repeated planning from scratch wastes structure shared with previously solved environments.
mechanism: Generate environment variants around stored trajectories, learn a solution-aware embedding with triplet loss, retrieve candidate paths, then collision-check or use them to bias classical planners.
evidence_scope: Three sampling-based planners, three procedural two-dimensional problem families, 30,000 held-out instances, memory-size variation, and random-retrieval ablation.
writing_move: Present a planner-agnostic interface, then distinguish closed-box path reuse from open-box changes to sampling and roadmap construction.
research_lesson: Test the cold-start regime and report when learning adds overhead before enough relevant experience accumulates.
reviewer_question: Do generated environments preserve feasibility or optimality, what is the cost of rebuilding memory, and how do changing goals or high-dimensional dynamics affect retrieval?

evidence_pages.observation: Start and goal have fixed separation and are aligned across problems.
Retrieved paths are collision-checked; unsupported optimization-based use is explicitly not evaluated.
20/40 stored plans underperform baseline; random retrieval worsens runtime.

limits_or_counterexample: The ablation establishes value over random retrieval, not necessity of this exact embedding or augmentation design. The broader universal-planner claim exceeds the three tested sampling-based planners; no physical deployment is evaluated.
citation: Dibyendu Das, Yuanjie Lu, Erion Plaku, and Xuesu Xiao . Motion Memory: Leveraging Past Experiences to Accelerate Future Motion Planning . 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA).
venue_full: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
research_line: Motion memory / experience reuse in planning

title: Scaling Team Coordination on Graphs with Reinforcement Learning
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read; equations not independently proved or code-audited
problem: Exact joint-state graph search becomes expensive as robot team size and graph connectivity grow.
mechanism: Encode robot positions, graph adjacency, and support costs in a centralized MDP; apply Q-learning/PPO with invalid-action masking and coordination-oriented reward shaping.
evidence_scope: Single-graph comparisons vary nodes, team size, and connectivity; reusable policies are separately evaluated for two agents on five/ten-node graphs.
writing_move: Split the deployment question into solving one instance versus amortizing training across future instances, then compare quality against solution time.
research_lesson: Expose crossover regimes where classical optimization remains better, and include both training and inference when the policy serves only one problem.
reviewer_question: Does discounted/shaped reward preserve the original traversal-cost objective, how is optimality ratio defined, and do unseen graph tests establish more than distribution-specific generalization?

evidence_pages.observation: Single-graph time includes RL training; multiple-graph deployment amortizes training.
Coordination reward is explicitly additional to the original traversal-cost objective.
JSG wins every two-agent case; all approaches fail the largest tested dense four-agent case.

limits_or_counterexample: Centralized full-graph access is assumed. Learned solutions are not guaranteed optimal; a policy evaluated on small sampled graph families is not a guarantee for every possible N-node graph.
citation: Manshi Limbu, Zechen Hu, Xuan Wang, Daigo Shishika, and Xuesu Xiao . Scaling Team Coordination on Graphs with Reinforcement Learning . 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA).
venue_full: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)

title: Rethinking Social Robot Navigation: Leveraging the Best of Two Worlds
reading_depth: Main text read in full; references not close-read
problem: Geometric planners handle many social scenes while imitation can help difficult ones but degrade under distribution shift.
mechanism: First audit geometric plan–demonstration alignment; learn a gating classifier and a behavior-cloning specialist for poorly aligned scenes, with deployment hysteresis and obstacle-triggered fallback.
evidence_scope: SCAND playback, manually curated out-of-distribution scenes, and repeated human-interaction trials with Jackal/Spot on two campuses.
writing_move: Lead with an empirical case study that questions an all-or-nothing modeling choice, then label the proposed hybrid as a proof of concept.
research_lesson: Validate an offline social proxy with human experience while preserving the distinction between geometric similarity and social appropriateness.
reviewer_question: Can multiple trajectories be socially acceptable, are participant-level repeated measures accounted for, and how much benefit comes from gating versus platform-specific safety engineering?

evidence_pages.observation: Hausdorff distance to one demonstration defines compliance, with explicit non-uniqueness caveat.
Hysteresis/fallback parameters are tuned per site/robot; hybrid is not best in every scenario.
BC sometimes needs intervention; authors retain engineering and baseline-simplicity limitations.

limits_or_counterexample: The approximately 80% alignment result depends on dataset and a one-meter threshold, not universal social compliance. Classical fallback and favorable ratings do not constitute a formal human-safety guarantee.
citation: Amir Hossain Raj, Zichao Hu, Haresh Karnan, Rohan Chandra, Amirreza Payandeh, Luisa Mao, Peter Stone, Joydeep Biswas, and Xuesu Xiao . Rethinking Social Robot Navigation: Leveraging the Best of Two Worlds . 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA).
venue_full: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
research_line: Social navigation: data, benchmarks, and language reasoning

title: Dexterous Legged Locomotion in Confined 3D Spaces with Reinforcement Learning
reading_depth: Main text read in full; PDF page 5 rendered to verify TablesII–IV; references not close-read
problem: Ground-focused velocity-tracking locomotion does not directly address all-around constraints in narrow three-dimensional spaces.
mechanism: A torso-only reactive pose sampler selects nearby goals; an RL joint controller learns goal-reaching with floor/ceiling height fields, retaining flexibility beyond predefined gait parameters.
evidence_scope: Procedural pyramid environments, 3000 simulation test trials, training-efficiency comparisons, and a controlled physical Go 1 demonstration.
writing_move: Reframe the missing capability as a mismatch between the training task and desired behavior, then compare three explicit formulations of that task.
research_lesson: A task-specific hierarchy can improve learning while changing the meaning of success: useful obstacle contact must not be misreported as collision-free navigation.
reviewer_question: Are contact forces/damage measured, do success-conditioned collision counts compare equivalent episodes, and how far does the physical demonstration test global navigation?

evidence_pages.observation: Planner checks only torso collision, providing rough rather than whole-body guidance.
On hard tasks hierarchy succeeds 39.4% versus 5.1% end-to-end, with 43.6 versus 29.8 contacts among successful trials.
Physical goal stays one meter ahead; artificial geometry and reactive planning remain limitations.

limits_or_counterexample: Higher contact counts are interpreted as obstacle-aided locomotion, not proven causal necessity. The simulated hierarchy still fails most hard trials; physical evidence is qualitative and not a distant-goal success-rate study.
citation: Zifan Xu, Amir Hossain Raj, Xuesu Xiao , and Peter Stone. Dexterous Legged Locomotion in Confined 3D Spaces with Reinforcement Learning . 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA).
venue_full: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)

title: MTG: Mapless Trajectory Generator with Traversability Coverage for Outdoor Navigation
reading_depth: Full main text on pages 1–7 read; external appendix not read; text-only review, no independent derivation verification.
problem: Mapless global navigation needs several traversable directions, not simply one collision-free local trajectory.
mechanism: A CVAE couples trajectory embeddings through attention and separately trains coverage, traversability, and diversity losses.
evidence_scope: Campus training/test areas, Husky and Spot deployments, comparisons with CVAE, DLOW, and a no-cross-trajectory-information variant. Coverage is a distance-derived proxy relative to A*-generated targets.
writing_move: Decomposes an apparently single performance objective into competing requirements and gives each requirement a method component and evaluation metric.
research_lesson: Diversity alone can be actively undesirable when valid routes are few; specify the useful diversity you want.
reviewer_question: Does reference-path coverage measure actual accessible directions under occlusion, and which gains survive a different map-derived labeling procedure?

evidence_pages.observation: Ground-truth trajectories are generated with A* on training maps.
Coverage, non-traversable fraction, diversity, and runtime are separately reported.

limits_or_counterexample: Mapless inference is not map-free training; learned penalties are not collision-avoidance proofs. Field of view limits candidate directions.
citation: Jing Liang, Peng Gao, Xuesu Xiao , Adarsh Jagan Sathyamoorthy, Mohamed Elnoor, Ming C. Lin, and Dinesh Manocha. MTG: Mapless Trajectory Generator with Traversability Coverage for Outdoor Navigation . 2024 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA).

title: Human Uncertainty-Aware MPC for Enhanced Human-Robot Collaborative Manipulation
reading_depth: Full main text on pages 1–6 read; derivation read but not independently verified; references not close-read.
problem: Co-manipulation tracking must accommodate biased human deviations from a nominal reference trajectory.
mechanism: Models positional deviations with a nonzero-mean Gaussian and derives an uncertainty-aware receding-horizon controller using modified Riccati recursions.
evidence_scope: Simulated Fetch-based eight-DOF configuration, three trajectories, two tracking weights, and three uncertainty scales, compared with uncertainty-ignorant MPC.
writing_move: Moves from an intuitive board-balancing scenario to explicit uncertainty assumptions, objective, theorem, algorithm, and controlled numerical validation.
research_lesson: A theoretical contribution needs assumptions and derivation matched to the exact operational claim; a parameter sweep can test behavior without inventing a human study.
reviewer_question: Which terms actually change the optimal action versus only the expected cost, and what happens under misspecified or changing human bias?

evidence_pages.observation: Assumes human uncertainty changes position but not reference orientation.
Derives control input and introduces simulated uncertainty-scaled tests.

limits_or_counterexample: No real human collaborative manipulation is demonstrated here; robot-model uncertainty is explicitly excluded.
citation: Al Jaber Mahmud, Duc M. Nguyen, Filipe Veiga, Xuesu Xiao , and Xuan Wang. Human Uncertainty-Aware MPC for Enhanced Human-Robot Collaborative Manipulation . 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems (ICPS). title: How susceptible are LLMs to Logical Fallacies?
reading_depth: Complete main text, limitations, and ethics sections read; references not close-read; no code replication.
problem: Single-turn answers cannot characterize how multi-round persuasion changes an LLM's expressed stance.
mechanism: LOGICOM compares no-helper, fallacious-helper, and logical-helper debates, with consistent main-agent prompts and LLM moderators that decide stance and termination.
evidence_scope: 100 topics with 200 opposing claims, three repetitions per scenario, July/August 2023 GPT snapshots; paired logical/fallacious arguments form a derived dataset.
writing_move: State two research questions, operationalize their distinct denominators, and add a matched helper control for the extra-agent explanation.
research_lesson: Define the psychological or reasoning construct cautiously when observable behavior is only a proxy; controls improve attribution without eliminating every prompt or judge confound.
reviewer_question: Are persuasion success and initially-disagreeing stance change separated, do human audits validate moderators/fallacy labels, and is the last fallacy causally responsible?

evidence_pages.observation: An extra logical-helper condition controls helper presence; automated moderators terminate debates.
RQ1 filters initially disagreeing debates, whereas RQ2 compares broader persuasion-success statistics.
Attributing influence to the last fallacy is an explicit analysis assumption.
Moderator errors, prompt sensitivity, few repeats, and limited model coverage are acknowledged.

limits_or_counterexample: Expressed agreement does not establish changed internal reasoning. Results are historical and prompt-dependent, and automated labels are not independent human validation.
citation: Amirreza Payandeh, Dan Pluth, Jordan Hosier, Xuesu Xiao , and Vijay K. Gurbani. How susceptible are LLMs to Logical Fallacies? . 2024 Joint International Conference on Computational Linguistics, Language Resources and Evaluation (LREC-COLING).
venue_full: 2024 Joint International Conference on Computational Linguistics, Language Resources and Evaluation (LREC-COLING)

title: Building Minimal and Reusable Causal State Abstractions for Reinforcement Learning
reading_depth: Complete main text and displayed theorem read; referenced external appendix not included in this PDF and not accessed; no independent proof or code verification.
problem: Reusable dynamics abstractions can retain irrelevant controllable variables and discard uncontrollable variables that matter to a reward.
mechanism: Infer reward dependencies and their dynamical ancestors, while improving implicit-model conditional-mutual-information estimation through score differences and regularization.
evidence_scope: Factored-state manipulation and DeepMind Control tasks; three seeds for dynamics and five for task learning, with graph accuracy, abstraction accuracy, return, and distractor-shift tests.
writing_move: Diagnose two distinct bottlenecks—task-specific relevance and inaccurate causal estimation—then evaluate intermediate quantities before final policy learning.
research_lesson: Hold the dynamics model and policy learner common when isolating abstraction quality; use an oracle to reveal headroom and a counterexample to explain predecessor limits.
reviewer_question: How reliable are causal dependencies under violated independence assumptions, and does robustness extend beyond changes to variables designated task-irrelevant?

evidence_pages.observation: Transitions are assumed factored; quaternion dependence is acknowledged as an empirical violation.
Conditional-model overfitting motivates using the full-minus-masked score.
All abstraction baselines use implicit dynamics and SAC; graph/abstraction tests use ground-truth reward dependencies.
OOD changes task-irrelevant variables to Gaussian noise; failed TIA/Denoised-MDP policies are excluded.

limits_or_counterexample: Factorized states are supplied, not learned from images. Theoretical bisimulation relies on assumptions beyond empirical graph accuracy; the OOD experiment is narrower than arbitrary dynamics or reward shift.

title: Visually Adaptive Geometric Navigation
reading_depth: Complete main text read; references not close-read; no code or parameter-safety proof audit.
problem: Geometry-only navigation misses semantic preferences, while low-data end-to-end visual control may fail at precise obstacle avoidance.
mechanism: Manually segment demonstrations into contexts, fit context-specific geometric-planner parameters with CMA-ES, and classify visual context online to select a parameter set.
evidence_scope: A 749-point semantic obstacle-course dataset and ten tests per method; a separately demonstrated/trained Spot-GraphNav implementation on a 200 m route.
writing_move: Make geometry and semantics disagree deliberately with identically shaped, differently colored obstacles; test a second planner/platform as a separate implementation.
research_lesson: Distinguish portability of a paradigm from zero-shot transfer of its trained policy, and include manual segmentation and parameter-optimization labor.
reviewer_question: Which parameter ranges preserve the planner's actual safety assumptions, and would end-to-end comparisons change with more data or matched expert tuning?

evidence_pages.observation: Context segmentation is manual; one parameter library is optimized from demonstrations.
Authors explicitly limit the small-data study to demonstrating a paradigm, not unseen-context generalization.
CMA-ES takes about six hours; the Spot deployment collects its own demonstration and trains again.
Generalizing the context predictor to unseen appearances remains future work.

limits_or_counterexample: Field results compare learned parameters with default GraphNav settings and do not establish a universal safety guarantee or cross-robot transfer without retraining.
citation: Shravan Ravi, Shreyas Satewar, Gary Wang, Xuesu Xiao , Garrett Warnell, Joydeep Biswas, and Peter Stone. Visually Adaptive Geometric Navigation . Accepted by 2023 IEEE International Symposium on Safety, Security, and Rescue Robotics (SSRR).

title: Toward Human-Like Social Robot Navigation: A Large-Scale, Multi-Modal, Social Human Navigation Dataset
reading_depth: Complete main text, anticipated uses, and conclusion read; references not close-read.
problem: Robot teleoperation is costly and ordinary human video lacks the robotic sensing needed to learn natural navigation interactions.
mechanism: A replicable helmet records LiDAR, stereo/depth, inertial, audio, and spherical video; odometry-derived velocities, smoothing, synchronization, and social-context tags support learning.
evidence_scope: Approximately 100 km / 20 h / 300 trajectories are reported; abstract/p. 2 say 13 demonstrators but methods p. 3 say 7. A ten-trajectory training subset supports qualitative BC demonstrations on two robot types.
writing_move: Compare complementary predecessor resources, justify each sensor by information supplied, and label downstream research ideas as anticipated rather than established.
research_lesson: Track whether a reported count denotes collected data, training examples, or independent evaluation; preserve source inconsistencies instead of silently resolving them.
reviewer_question: What is the reconciled demonstrator count, how are consent/privacy and annotation agreement handled, and which embodiment/viewpoint shifts are actually validated?

evidence_pages.observation: Dataset summary reports 13 demonstrators; collection procedure on p. 3 reports 7.
Velocities are inferred from odometry rather than human action commands; gait creates sensor mismatch.
Ten navigation trials are used to TRAIN BC; no physical evaluation trial count is given here.
Human–robot behavioral equivalence and socially preferred behavior are posed as research questions.

limits_or_counterexample: Collision-avoidance illustrations do not establish social compliance or validate every proposed use. A human trajectory need not be the appropriate trajectory for a differently embodied robot.

title: Team Coordination on Graphs with State-Dependent Edge Costs
reading_depth: Complete main text, algorithms, and displayed proof read for argument and assumptions; references not close-read; no independent proof/code verification.
problem: Independent shortest paths ignore supportive actions that reduce a teammate's traversal cost.
mechanism: Encode joint positions and support-dependent costs in a joint-state graph; retain critical support-start/end configurations and compose independent shortest paths between them.
evidence_scope: A two-agent deterministic formulation with a path-preservation argument, complexity analysis, and graph-construction/search timings across node counts and support densities.
writing_move: Introduce an understandable ladder-support example, formalize costs, then align scaling experiments with the structure responsible for compression.
research_lesson: Preserve decision-coupling events while simplifying independent segments; show the regime where the compressed representation approaches the original size.
reviewer_question: Do zero-cost waiting, synchronized path composition, graph sparsity, and support assumptions hold in the intended application, and how does scaling change with more agents?

evidence_pages.observation: Risk is modeled as deterministic traversal cost, not probability of physical failure.
Shorter component paths are padded by staying at their final node; the proof connects critical states.
Savings diminish as critical states approach all joint states; construction and search costs are reported separately.

limits_or_counterexample: The abstraction does not model generic robot collisions, stochastic hazards, or communication imperfections. 'No worse' asymptotic order is not a claim that every measured runtime must be smaller.

title: Benchmarking Reinforcement Learning Techniques for Autonomous Navigation
reading_depth: Complete main text and tables read; references not close-read; externally linked implementation supplements not accessed.
problem: Navigation learning techniques need common tests tied to partial observability, safety, sample efficiency, and generalization.
mechanism: Construct static, random-moving-box, and structured-moving-wall tasks; compare memory architectures, Lagrangian safety, model-based methods, and environmental diversity under shared TD3 settings.
evidence_scope: 500 generated environments with held-out sets, three independent training runs, and six selected systems tested three times in each of three physical settings.
writing_move: Turn four desiderata into an experimental taxonomy, and report negative findings when expected learning benefits fail to appear.
research_lesson: Memory helps when history predicts a decision-relevant hazard, not automatically whenever obstacles move; additional modeling need not improve low-data learning.
reviewer_question: Does unsuccessful-episode survival distinguish collision avoidance from immobility, are model and rollout budgets comparable, and do three physical repeats support a stable ranking?

evidence_pages.observation: Longer history can hurt; survival time includes collision-terminated and time-limit failures.
Memory helps structured moving walls more than random boxes; model-based methods do not win low-data comparisons.
MPC fails all three large-scale physical trials; broader-domain MLP succeeds in all nine physical tests.

limits_or_counterexample: These are tested methods and procedural regimes, not universal laws about model-based RL. Long survival and a safety-oriented loss are not formal safety or liveness guarantees.
citation: Zifan Xu, Bo Liu, Xuesu Xiao , Anirudh Nair, and Peter Stone. Benchmarking Reinforcement Learning Techniques for Autonomous Navigation . 2023 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA).

title: Learning Perceptual Hallucination for Multi-Robot Navigation in Narrow Hallways
reading_depth: Complete main text and tables read; references not close-read; no code replication.
problem: Two robots using static-environment navigation stacks may collide, stop, or turn around when passing in narrow corridors.
mechanism: Optimize static virtual obstacle fields with CMA-ES and domain-randomized simulation; inject the minimum of real and virtual laser ranges into the existing planner.
evidence_scope: I/L training, transfer among hallway shapes, communication-dropout tests, and 192 physical episodes across six geometry/robot-asymmetry conditions.
writing_move: Modify a narrow perception interface, then stress the exact coordination assumptions with differing speed, detection range, and learned obstacle fields.
research_lesson: Reducing the frequency or precision of required information can be a practical contribution without eliminating communication entirely.
reviewer_question: How much localization/detection is required to initialize the field, what happens with nonparticipating robots, and do conservative virtual obstacles preserve progress?

evidence_pages.observation: Both robots have global plans and approximate knowledge of the other's position; only additional virtual obstacles are allowed.
Training takes about 20 h on a roughly 150-node cluster; low-dimensional inference should not obscure this cost.
Robots exchange locations over WiFi; 192 episodes have no collisions/turnarounds, but only two PHHP-equipped robots are tested.

limits_or_counterexample: Static scan augmentation and observed collision-free trials do not prove safety with arbitrary moving agents. Both participants use compatible hallucinations; zero communication and unrestricted fleet scalability are not demonstrated.
citation: Jin-Soo Park, Xuesu Xiao , Garrett Warnell, Harel Yedidsion, and Peter Stone. Learning Perceptual Hallucination for Multi-Robot Navigation in Narrow Hallways . 2023 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA).

title: Learning Model Predictive Controllers with Real-Time Attention for Real-World Navigation
reading_depth: Complete main text pp. 1–8 and selected appendix pp. 18–20 read; appendix derivations/settings pp. 15–17 and detailed result tables pp. 21–22 not fully read; references not close-read.
problem: Context-dependent navigation costs need expressive perception without making online MPC prohibitively slow.
mechanism: Learn an occupancy-grid-conditioned residual quadratic cost through bilevel imitation with implicit differentiation; retain hand-designed costs and a secondary nonlearned tracking MPC.
evidence_scope: One simulated doorway task, physical constrained navigation, two social scenarios, and separate runtime studies; social pilot uses nine research-team members in 120 sessions.
writing_move: Connect efficient attention and cost parameterization to operational timing, then explicitly limit the social study's inferential strength.
research_lesson: Distinguish architecture, optimization, training distribution, and human-study claims; scenario-specific recovery demonstrations and background augmentation are part of the method.
reviewer_question: What does the full deployed latency include, how do learned and retained costs interact, and do repeated questionnaires justify the claimed social effect?

evidence_pages.observation: The policy includes a tracking MPC; learned residual costs augment a user-engineered cost.
CPU versus wall-clock timing differ; spatial occupancy-grid attention and separately trained scenario costs limit scope.
Background augmentation targets memorized building layouts; social norms used for training also guide evaluation.
N=9, 120 sessions, 240 questionnaires; authors explicitly reject statistically significant causal interpretation of this unbalanced pilot.

limits_or_counterexample: This is not a general multi-scenario RGB-language controller. Convex quadratic residuals do not make nonlinear MPC globally optimal, and descriptive pilot scores do not establish population-wide social preference.
citation: Xuesu Xiao , Tingnan Zhang, Krzysztof Choromanski, Edward Lee, Anthony Francis, Jake Varley, Stephen Tu, Sumeet Singh, Peng Xu, Fei Xia, Sven Mikael Persson, Dmitry Kalashnikov, Leila Takayama, Roy Frostig, Jie Tan, Carolina Parada, and Vikas Sindhwani. Learning Model Predictive Controllers with Real-Time Attention for Real-World Navigation . 2022 Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL).

title: DynaBARN: Benchmarking Metric Ground Navigation in Dynamic Environments
reading_depth: Complete main text, including conclusion continuation on p. 6, read; references not close-read.
problem: Dynamic-obstacle benchmarks using one motion model under-test variation in speed, turning, and temporal predictability.
mechanism: Generate cylindrical obstacle waypoint paths with polynomial geometry and bounded variable speeds; expose motion-profile and obstacle-count controls plus a teleoperation pipeline.
evidence_scope: 300 generated worlds; four baselines on 60 selected environments, ten tests per environment. RL uses 20M steps per difficulty and is evaluated on its training environments.
writing_move: Specify the generative procedure and difficulty knobs before baseline results, and disclose unequal data exposure when interpreting rankings.
research_lesson: A benchmark generator can be useful without showing held-out generalization; label in-environment performance correctly and avoid importing broader transfer claims.
reviewer_question: Do parameterized difficulty levels predict failures across planners, what train/test overlap is intended, and how would reciprocal or differently shaped obstacles change outcomes?

evidence_pages.observation: Obstacles follow predetermined waypoints and do not react to the robot.
Baseline evaluation selects 60 of 300 worlds; two coauthors provide demonstration trajectories.
RL tests in the same environments used for training; the authors attribute part of its advantage to 20M-step exposure.

limits_or_counterexample: Success is the sole reported metric; smoothness and timing are future additions. Cylindrical nonreactive motion is not a model of reciprocal human social navigation or unseen-world reliability.
citation: Anirudh Nair, Fulin Jiang, Kang Hou, Zifan Xu, Shuozhe Li, Xuesu Xiao , and Peter Stone. DynaBARN: Benchmarking Metric Ground Navigation in Dynamic Environments . 2022 IEEE International Symposium on Safety, Security, and Rescue Robotics (SSRR).

title: High-Speed Accurate Robot Control using Learned Forward Kinodynamics and Non-linear Least Squares Optimization
reading_depth: Complete main text and displayed formulation read; references not close-read; probability/optimization derivations not independently verified.
problem: Inverse-dynamics trajectory queries require feasible reference sequences and are awkward to reuse for new control objectives.
mechanism: Learn multi-step forward kinodynamics recurrently and optimize a nonlinear least-squares control objective, with asynchronous state estimation, optimization, latency-aware update, and execution.
evidence_scope: A one-tenth-scale car follows two paths at several speeds with five traversals per speed, then demonstrates a start-to-goal time/distance objective against an IKD controller following human racing lines.
writing_move: Present a reusable mathematical interface, explain why naïve one-step training is insufficient, and connect its implementation to timestamped control buffers.
research_lesson: Separate predictive knowledge from objective choice; test model architecture/data/training equivalence while disclosing different online optimization and reference inputs.
reviewer_question: Does the optimizer exploit model extrapolation, are timing/state-estimation assumptions validated, and is 'time-optimal' a global guarantee or a weighted local objective?

evidence_pages.observation: Block recurrent prediction preserves fine temporal resolution without 60 sequential model calls.
Updater discards controls made stale by estimation and optimization latency.
FKD/IKD share network architecture, data, and training iterations.
The connectivity example compares an optimized route with an IKD-tracked human route; lower-dimensional coverage is offered as an explanation.

limits_or_counterexample: The comparison supports this implementation, not universal FKD superiority. A faster demonstrated route and weighted endpoint/time cost are not proof of globally minimum-time control.

title: VI-IKD: High-Speed Accurate Off-Road Navigation using Learned Visual-Inertial Inverse Kinodynamics
reading_depth: Full main text, PDF pp. 1–7, including formulation, implementation, indoor/outdoor evaluation, conclusion, and future work. References not close-read; no code replication.
problem: Inertial history describes terrain already encountered, but high-speed control needs to anticipate terrain reached after actuation delay.
mechanism: Learn an inverse kinodynamic model conditioned on inertial history and a viewpoint-aligned visual patch selected for the predicted future contact location.
evidence_scope: One 1/5-scale Ackermann vehicle; 60 minutes of teleoperation for learning; 270 indoor laps across methods/speeds and ten outdoor laps per method. Visual encoding uses an off-board laptop GPU.
writing_move: Turn the sensing-delay mismatch into a precise reason for adding vision, then test on explicit terrain transitions.
research_lesson: Match anticipatory information to execution timing; document compute placement and define the evaluation unit before interpreting success.
reviewer_question: Does the benefit persist on unseen terrain, without localization aids or off-board compute, and under latency error?

evidence_pages.observation: The patch-extraction pipeline accounts for future position; the visual encoder runs off-board on an RTX 2060 laptop at 40 Hz.
The same collected data train both learned models; indoor localization uses added fixtures, and Table I reports turn success counts.
Failed outdoor turns are reset before continuation; VI-IKD completes all ten loops without failure. Unseen-terrain performance remains future work.

limits_or_counterexample: Outdoor baseline turn counts are not uninterrupted route-success counts because failed runs resume after resets. The controller uses a one-step horizon; tested heterogeneous terrain is not proof of novel-terrain generalization.
citation: Haresh Karnan, Kavan Singh Sikand, Pranav Atreya, Sadegh Rabiee, Xuesu Xiao , Garrett Warnell, Peter Stone, and Joydeep Biswas. VI-IKD: High-Speed Accurate Off-Road Navigation using Learned Visual-Inertial Inverse Kinodynamics . 2022 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS).
venue_full: 2022 IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)

title: Causal Dynamics Learning for Task-Independent State Abstraction
reading_depth: Full main text, PDF pp. 1–9, including assumptions, theorem statement, architecture, exploration, experiments, and conclusion. References and appendices/proofs pp. 10–30 not closely read or independently verified.
problem: Dense dynamics encode unnecessary dependencies, while reward-specific abstractions can discard variables needed by later tasks.
mechanism: Estimate conditional mutual information using shared masked predictors, infer causal parents, and retain controllable variables plus their ancestors; collect informative transitions with prediction-difference rewards.
evidence_scope: Chemical and simulated manipulation domains; three seeds, 5,000 prediction-test transitions, and 100 downstream evaluation episodes per condition. OOD tests shift selected nuisance-variable distributions.
writing_move: Give an intuitive door-and-clock example, formalize the admissible task family and causal assumptions, then state five experimentally addressable hypotheses.
research_lesson: A reusable abstraction requires an explicit preservation contract: specify which future rewards and distribution shifts it supports.
reviewer_question: Are faithfulness, full observability, independent next-variable transitions, and sufficient exploration plausible, and how sensitive is the learned graph to the per-environment CMI threshold?

evidence_pages.observation: Actively-accomplishable tasks exclude rewards depending on action-irrelevant variables; a clock-gated door reward is the explicit counterexample. Theorem 3.1 assumes A1–A5.
CMI thresholds vary across environments; manipulation exploration uses supplied long-horizon skills. OOD tests change object or marker positions, evaluating other variables.
Dynamics are frozen while learning new reward predictors; four downstream tasks and matched transition counts separate several proposed benefits.

limits_or_counterexample: Task-independent does not mean any reward: CDL can discard uncontrollable but reward-relevant context. The theory does not directly guarantee a finite-data learned graph, image-state performance, or robustness to arbitrary causal-mechanism shifts.
citation: Zizhao Wang, Xuesu Xiao , Zifan Xu, Yuke Zhu, and Peter Stone. Causal Dynamics Learning for Task-Independent State Abstraction . 2022 International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML).
venue_full: 2022 International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML)

title: VOILA: Visual-Observation-Only Imitation Learning for Autonomous Navigation
reading_depth: Full main text, PDF pp. 1–6. References and the separately referenced extended version were not close-read; no implementation replication.
problem: Action-labeled demonstrations on the deployment robot are costly; human video has both missing controls and viewpoint mismatch.
mechanism: Use off-the-shelf keypoint match density to construct an imitation reward, then train a reactive policy with SAC; demonstration images supply training rewards, not test-time retrieval.
evidence_scope: AirSim road following trains on two tracks and evaluates twelve with five trials each. Physical hallway training uses one human video but 120 robot episodes over 90 minutes, including manual resets.
writing_move: Formulate a concrete missing-supervision scenario, separate two research questions, and distinguish viewpoint robustness from environmental transfer.
research_lesson: Report the full learning interaction budget: one demonstration is not one-shot autonomous deployment or zero human involvement.
reviewer_question: How robust is the reward to repetitive or textureless scenes, and do results survive beyond straight simulated roads and a perturbed version of the same building?

evidence_pages.observation: Training terminates on crashes or fewer than ten keypoint matches; real crashes are trainer-detected. After initialization, retrieval searches the next three expert frames.
Two training and ten unseen tracks; shared representation, but GAIfO receives one million steps versus VOILA's 100,000.
The robot is manually reset after training episodes; physical transfer repositions objects in the original environment, with no repeated-test sample size stated.

limits_or_counterexample: The expert video is action-free, not the robot's learning process. Physical environmental perturbation is narrower than new-building generalization, and real-world collision-free demonstrations do not establish a safety guarantee.
citation: Haresh Karnan, Garrett Warnell, Xuesu Xiao , and Peter Stone. VOILA: Visual-Observation-Only Imitation Learning for Autonomous Navigation . 2022 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA).
venue_full: 2022 IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation (ICRA)
